clue.text: For each boy a large kind of computer

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'ten pounds per head'
a son is a boy
taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A shopper picks out a big computer for each of their boys.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal computer, or PC, is the type of machine built for one individual's use.

clue.text: Exhibits, for example, as central idea in show

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the word that follows it

parts.note: to evince is to show or display a quality

indicators.note: central asks for the letters at the heart of the following word, dropping its ends

parts.note: the two middle letters of the four-letter word

explanation.surface: A critic notes that some exhibits embody the central idea of an art show.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle pair of idea sits inside EVINCE after its third letter: EVI-DE-NCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhibits in a trial are items of proof put before the court, an example of what a court weighs.

clue.text: Blocking or playing for time — nothing novel in that

indicators.note: in that tells us the preceding pieces sit inside the word the clue just described

parts.note: stalling is delaying to gain time
nothing is zero, the letter O
novel as an adjective means new

explanation.surface: Someone describes a defensive tactic, blocking or stalling, and says there is nothing new about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing for time' looks like a second definition, but it is the outer word of the wordplay. Stonewalling is also cricket slang for dour defensive batting.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonewalling is obstructing or refusing to cooperate, which is a form of deliberate blocking.

clue.text: Heavenly drink producing trance when drunk

indicators.note: something drunk is reeling and disordered, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: the six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A divine beverage sends whoever drinks it into a trance.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar was the drink of the gods in Greek myth, hence a heavenly beverage.

clue.text: Vehicle's fuel used up covering motorway

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards
covering means wrapping around the next item, holding it inside

parts.note: oil is a fuel
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A car has run out of fuel on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: Turned upwards, OIL becomes LIO, which then wraps M: LI-M-O.
explanation.definitionFit: A limo, short for limousine, is a large luxury car, so a vehicle.

clue.text: Yellow arch spanning part of hospital on left

indicators.note: spanning means stretching across and around what follows, enclosing it

parts.note: arch as an adjective means slyly playful, which is coy
a ward is a section of a hospital
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A yellow arched structure spans a hospital wing on its left side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arch' looks like a noun for a structure; here it is the adjective meaning coy, which wraps WARD and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is informal for lacking courage, the same as being timid or craven.

clue.text: What's at centre of nasty eye?

definitions.text: What's at centre of nasty eye?

indicators.note: at centre of tells us the letters sit in the middle of the words that follow, across their join

parts.note: the letters straddling the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Someone asks what is causing the soreness in the middle of an inflamed eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the answer is literally inside the phrase and is the thing an infected eye might have.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a nasty thing found on the eye.

clue.text: Do some needlework over time, note

indicators.note: over means lying across and around what follows, so it is enclosed

parts.note: to crochet is to make fabric with a hooked needle
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A reminder note to do some sewing again later.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes into the needlework verb after its fourth letter: CRO-T-CHET.
explanation.definitionFit: A crotchet is a musical note lasting one beat, the British name for a quarter note.

clue.text: My off-putting statement for someone not in good faith?

parts.note: surface reading: an exclamation followed by a remark that delays a chore
setter's reading: the answer split as three words is the procrastinator's line 'I'll do it later', and whole it names a worshipper of false gods

explanation.surface: A procrastinator's excuse is offered as a sign of bad faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as I DO LATER, the answer is the off-putting promise; read whole, it is a person whose faith is in idols rather than the true God.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater worships images or false gods, so their religious faith is misplaced by orthodox standards.

clue.text: Short measure for Juliet's follower

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the clipped form of kilogram, a unit of weight
second meaning: the code word after Juliet in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A small drink is poured for whoever is chasing Shakespeare's Juliet.
explanation.walkthrough: Juliet suggests Romeo, but she is the J of the radio alphabet, and K comes next.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilo abbreviates kilogram, and in radio spelling it stands for the letter K, which follows J.

clue.text: Financial problem for people in land to beat somehow

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are arranged in a way we must work out

parts.note: the twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A country's citizens face a money worry they must somehow overcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A national debt is the total a government owes, a fiscal burden borne by its citizens.

clue.text: Account in personal record that's distracting

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the one that follows it

parts.note: a diary is a private daily record
a version is one person's account of events

explanation.surface: A diary entry turns out to be a red herring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Account' suggests a bank, but here it is someone's telling of events.
explanation.definitionFit: Diversionary describes something intended to draw attention away, which is what distracting means.

clue.text: As herald of spring, wintry weather event?

definitions.text: As herald of spring, wintry weather event?

parts.note: straight reading: an early flower that announces spring
setter's reading: the name split in two describes a fall of frozen flakes

explanation.walkthrough: The flower's name read as two words, a snow drop, sounds like a weather report; the question mark flags this play.
explanation.definitionFit: The snowdrop is a small white bulb flower that blooms in late winter, traditionally a sign that spring is near.

clue.text: Irritating person ending with love — that's saucy

definitions.note: a noun clause: the thing that is a sauce

indicators.note: ending with tells us which piece comes last in the line-up

parts.note: a pest is an annoying person
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: An annoying person ends a message with love, which seems rather cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saucy' looks like it means cheeky, but here it means sauce-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian sauce of basil, pine nuts and cheese, so a thing that is a sauce.

clue.text: Party opposing one call for peace is not this

definitions.text: Party opposing one call for peace is not this

parts.note: a do is a party
V, for versus, means against or opposing
I is the Roman numeral one
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A political party that rejects a ceasefire plea can hardly be called peace-loving.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a party that opposes a call for peace is the opposite of the answer. 'Peace' here is peace and quiet, hence SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Dovish means favouring negotiation over force, like the dove, the bird that symbolises conciliation.

clue.text: Daily fare from Tallahassee, Florida fell, finally

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of each of the words before it

parts.note: the final letter of this word
the final letter of the Florida city
the final letter of the state
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A newspaper item reports that a Florida city's everyday food bill dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' looks like a link word, but its last letter is the first of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A meal is the food eaten at one sitting, the regular fare served each day.

clue.text: Intervene to contain cold, administer dose

indicators.note: to contain means to hold inside, so the next item is enclosed

parts.note: to mediate is to intervene in a dispute
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A doctor steps in to stop a cold spreading and hands out medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes into MEDIATE after its fourth letter: MEDI-C-ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To medicate is to treat a patient with drugs, which means giving them a dose.

clue.text: Evaluate a second opinion

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second
one's say is one's opinion, as in 'have your say'

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to assess something by seeking a second opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second opinion' reads as a fixed phrase, but second gives only S.
explanation.definitionFit: To assay is to test or analyse, especially metal for purity, which is a form of evaluation.

clue.text: More than anything else, duck meat in lab going bad

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces inside the word that follows
going bad means spoiling, so the letters of the word before are disordered

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, the letter O
veal is calf meat

explanation.surface: Above all, a lab should not let its duck meat go off.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck is the cricket term for a score of nothing, a common source of O.
explanation.definitionFit: Above all is an idiom meaning most importantly, before every other consideration.

clue.text: Break balance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pause from work
second meaning: what remains, the remainder

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like a snooker or tennis phrase, but they are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest is a short pause from activity, and 'the rest' is whatever amount is left over.

clue.text: Allow to go ahead or punitively try to stop

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to give official approval
second meaning: to impose penalties on a state or person

explanation.surface: A government weighs whether to approve something or penalise it.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is one of English's self-opposites: it can mean both permit and penalise.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction is to authorise formally, and also to impose penalties such as trade embargoes to deter behaviour.

clue.text: Piece in game removed from board, ominously

indicators.note: removed from means taken out of the words that follow, lifted from within them

parts.note: the letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A game piece is taken off the board in a threatening way.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is one of the spotted tiles used in the game of dominoes.

clue.text: Biddable? Constrained by old inclination, pass

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: constrained by means held in by something, so the last item sits inside the one before it

parts.note: a bent is a natural inclination or talent
to pass away is to die

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an old habit that keeps them in line counts as obedience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' tempts as a definition of letting go by; it is the euphemism for dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Biddable means willing to do as one is bid or told, which is compliant.

clue.text: Mystery in game, possibly, e.g. man I exchanged

indicators.note: exchanged means swapped about, so the letters change places

parts.note: the six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: In a game, one man swaps places with another, leaving an unsolved puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In game, possibly' is a bonus: those letters rearrange to the answer too, so the clue holds two anagrams of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a puzzling person or thing, a riddle that defies explanation.

clue.text: Flock mistakenly got grain once

indicators.note: mistakenly means in error, so the letters come out in the wrong order

parts.note: the twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A flock of birds once got hold of grain by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flock' suggests sheep or birds; here it is a church's people.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister's flock is a figurative term for the worshippers gathered in a church.

clue.text: Standard choice between central characters for us

wordplay.words: choice between central characters for us
wordplay.note: A choice between the two letters at the middle of our alphabet

explanation.surface: A conventional choice made between the main characters in our story.
explanation.walkthrough: M and N are the 13th and 14th of our 26 letters, and 'N or M' is also the placeholder name in the Anglican catechism.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is the accepted standard or usual pattern against which things are measured.

clue.text: A container that's not closed

parts.note: taken as written
a jar is a container

explanation.surface: A storage pot has been left with its lid off.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajar describes a door or lid slightly open, so not fully shut.

clue.text: Landed, advanced, and fired

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
lit means set alight, as a fire is

explanation.surface: A rocket touched down, moved forward and launched.
explanation.definitionFit: Alit is an old past tense of alight, meaning came down to rest, as a bird does.

clue.text: Food for Mexicans I will put in wrong area

indicators.note: put in means inserted, so this item is placed inside the following ones

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
I will contracts to I'll
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A cook vows to make a dish for Mexican guests, but in the wrong place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' reads as an adjective with area; it is the legal noun tort, and ILL goes between it and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla is a thin flatbread of maize or wheat, a staple of Mexican cooking.

clue.text: Preparing last piece of poetry in literary event

indicators.note: in puts the selected letter inside the item that follows

parts.note: a reading is an event where an author reads their work aloud

indicators.note: last piece of asks for only the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A poet is getting ready to perform the final part of their verse at a book event.
explanation.definitionFit: Readying means making ready, which is the same as getting something prepared.
